rows.letter:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Garden Road crossing

We measured activity at Garden Road crossing from video of 34.8 minutes, using SAM tracking and post-encroachment time. In that period there were 25 crossings and 13 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 56.9 km/h. We recorded 6 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, with 3 where the person was first and 3 where the vehicle was first.

The worst cases were: One serious near-miss had a gap of 0.2 s with a car at 58.2 km/h and an adult death risk of 16.0% if hit by a car front. Another serious near-miss had a gap of 1.1 s with a motorcycle at 31.2 km/h and an adult death risk of 1.6% if hit by a car front. Another serious near-miss had a gap of 0.1 s with a bus at 27.2 km/h and an adult death risk of 1.2% if hit by a car front. Another serious near-miss had a gap of 0.7 s with a van at 25.7 km/h and an adult death risk of 1.0% if hit by a car front. Another serious near-miss had a gap of 0.7 s with a car at 22.3 km/h and an adult death risk of 0.7% if hit by a car front. Death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 43 pedestrians and 22 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 34.8 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice. Also, 51.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, with 12 gaps and longest gap 8.1 s, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you provide a raised zebra crossing with speed table and 20 km/h zone markings and signs at this location. We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

rows.letter:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at North Avenue crossing

We write to request a raised zebra crossing at the North Avenue crossing used by our school.

A Crossing Watch video recorded 7.6 minutes (456.0 s) at the site and counted 9 pedestrian crossings and 12 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 59.7 km/h.

In that recording 4 of 9 crossings (1 in 2.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 2 of 9 (1 in 4.5) within 1.5 s. If this recording is typical, exact 95% ranges are 13.7-78.8% and 2.8-60.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Of the 4 events within 3 s, 2 were serious (less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 were close passes (1.5-3.0 s).

One serious event had a car at 51.1 km/h with 0.3 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot.
That speed carries an adult death risk of 9.1% if hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+), compared with 0.6% at an impact speed of 20.0 km/h.
A second serious event had a van at 27.7 km/h with 1.3 s between pedestrian and vehicle.
That speed carries an adult death risk of 1.2% if hit, compared with 0.2% at 10.0 km/h.
One close pass had a bus at 57.0 km/h with 2.2 s between pedestrian and vehicle.
That speed carries an adult death risk of 2.3% if hit.
A second close pass had a car at 19.7 km/h with 1.8 s between pedestrian and vehicle.
That speed carries an adult death risk of 0.2% if hit, compared with 0.2% at 9.5 km/h.
The time gaps are post-encroachment times from SAM tracking and road-plane geometry, and the individual road user was not reviewed.

The video also showed 43.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 10 gaps with 4 of them 12 s or more and the longest 82.5 s.
We note the first and last gaps are cut short by the video, and that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video while this recording is 7.6 minutes with 9 crossings and 12 vehicles, so those rates should be treated with caution.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location to slow traffic and establish priority for pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and underlying measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Canal Road crossing

During 44.2 minutes of video we observed 18 crossings and 14 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 44.9 km/h and there were 7 gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed.

We define serious as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass as 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart.

A second event was a close pass with a gap of 2.0 s involving an auto-rickshaw travelling at 43.5 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front would be 1.3%.

A third event was a close pass with a gap of 2.8 s involving a car travelling at 29.6 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front would be 0.0%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 based on 24 pedestrians and 19 moving vehicles an hour, scaled from 44.2 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour, and 96.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location.

We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

rows.letter:
To the Road Authority
Subject: Request for safety improvement at Hill View Road crossing

Dear Sir or Madam,

Our school commissioned a Crossing Watch analysis of the Hill View Road crossing covering 40.2 minutes (2412.0 s) of video.
The analysis recorded 27 crossings and 16 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 53.4 km/h.
There were 4 serious near-misses defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and 2 close passes defined as 1.5 to 3.0 s apart.
Of the events, 2 were person first, 3 were vehicle first and 1 was both at once.
There were 10 gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed and 3 gaps of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 38.0 s.

The worst events were as follows.
The most severe serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with a motorcycle at 51.2 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front would be 9.1% and would be 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A second serious near-miss had a PET of 0.9 s with a car at 47.9 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front would be 7.0% and would be 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h.
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 0.3 s with an auto-rickshaw at 47.3 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front would be 6.6% and would be 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A fourth serious near-miss had a PET of 0.6 s with a motorcycle at 24.7 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front would be 0.9% and would be 0.6% at an impact of 20.0 km/h.
A close pass had a PET of 1.5 s with an auto-rickshaw at 46.5 km/h, where the adult death risk if hit by a car front would be 6.2% and would be 0.0% at an impact of 0.0 km/h.
Risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 from 40 pedestrians and 24 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 40.2 minutes of video, with the caveat that a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can double-count by 1.3x in drone tests.
Also 83.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with the caveat that the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing at this location.
We would be pleased to share the video and the full Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Road Authority Officer,

Over 5.2 minutes (312.0 s) of video at Hill View Road crossing we recorded 7 pedestrian crossings and 18 moving vehicles.

4 of 7 crossings (1 in 1.8) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, and 2 of 7 (1 in 3.5) within 1.5 s.

The 85th percentile speed was 51.3 km/h.

The most severe serious near-miss involved a van at 44.5 km/h with 1.4 s separation, with an adult death risk if hit of 5.2% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A second serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 28.0 km/h with 0.8 s separation, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.2%.

A close pass involved a car at 46.6 km/h with 2.3 s separation, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.5%.

Another close pass involved a van at 30.9 km/h with 2.1 s separation, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.2%.

PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video, while this recording is 5.2 minutes.

97.2% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 8 such gaps, 0 of them 12 s or more, and longest 10.6 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce approach speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

rows.letter:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Market Street crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We are writing as the school using Market Street crossing. We commissioned video monitoring of the crossing.

Measurements were made by Crossing Watch using SAM tracking, road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time. The video covered 16.6 minutes (996.0 s). In that time 26 crossings and 41 vehicles were recorded. The 85th percentile speed was 53.2 km/h.

There were 4 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 2 close passes, defined as 1.5-3.0 s apart. Of the near-misses, 3 were person-first, 2 were vehicle-first and 1 was both at once.

The worst events were as follows. One serious near-miss involved a car at 54.0 km/h with a gap of 1.1 s, with an adult death risk if hit of 11.5% per Rosen & Sander 2009 for adults 15+ hit by a car front.
Another serious near-miss involved a van at 43.9 km/h with a gap of 1.2 s, with an adult death risk if hit of 5.0% per the same source.
Another serious near-miss involved a van at 28.5 km/h with a gap of 0.0 s, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.3% per the same source.
Another serious near-miss involved a car at 26.6 km/h with a gap of 1.0 s, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.1% per the same source.
One close pass involved a van at 36.8 km/h with a gap of 1.8 s, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.3% per the same source.

For context, PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 94 pedestrians and 148 vehicles an hour scaled from 16.6 minutes of video, though a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can overcount by 1.3x in our drone test. Also, 93.0% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with 7 gaps, 5 of them 12 s or more, longest 68.6 s, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you provide a raised zebra crossing at this location.

We would be pleased to share the video and data for your review and to discuss next steps.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

rows.letter:
Dear Sir/Madam,

Re: Safety at North Avenue crossing

We write on behalf of the school regarding the crossing outside our premises. A Crossing Watch review of 30.3 minutes (1818.0 s) of video at North Avenue crossing recorded 17 crossings and 11 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 40.8 km/h. In that period 2 of 17 crossings (1 in 8.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person, of which 1 of 17 (1 in 17) was within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges, if this recording is typical, are 1.5-36.4% and 0.1-28.7% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson).

The most serious near-miss had a gap of 1.0 s between the person and a bus travelling at 36.8 km/h. Rosén & Sander 2009 estimates that an adult hit by a car front at that speed has a 2.7% death risk, compared with 0.2% death risk at an impact of 7.5 km/h if limited to 20 km/h. A second close pass had a gap of 2.9 s from a bus travelling at 28.3 km/h.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8 scaled from 30.3 minutes of video, but a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count 1.3x the true count in our drone test. In the recording, 47.3% of time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, comprising 8 gaps including 6 of 12 s or more with longest 13.6 s, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with a raised table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give priority to people crossing.

We hold the video and tracking data and would be pleased to share them for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

rows.letter:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lake View Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

As Principal of the school by the Lake View Road crossing I write to request safety improvements based on video measurements.

We observed the crossing for 18.8 minutes (1128.0 s) and recorded 5 crossings and 7 vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 44.1 km/h.

By definition a serious near-miss is a pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and a close pass is 1.5 s to 3.0 s apart.

We recorded 1 serious near-miss and 1 close pass, with 2 cases where the person went first.

The most serious event was a car passing 0.8 s after a pedestrian at 21.3 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk at that speed would be 0.7% and at an impact of 20.0 km/h it would be 0.6% per Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

The second event was a car passing 1.8 s after a pedestrian at 39.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front the death risk at that speed would be 1.6% and at an impact of 0.0 km/h it would be 0.0%.

For context the video scales to PV² of 0.0 x 10^8 from 16 pedestrians and 22 moving vehicles an hour, though a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one twice at 1.3x the true count in our drone test.

About 66.9% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, comprising 9 gaps of which 5 were 12 s or more with a longest gap of 72.5 s, though the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce speeds and provide priority for pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
Approved by The Principal

rows.letter:
To the Road Authority,

I write on behalf of the school at the Orchard Lane crossing.

A 2.0 minute video recorded seven pedestrian crossings and 22 vehicles, with 85th percentile speed 63.3 km/h.

In that recording 5 of 7 crossings (1 in 1.4) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s and 3 of 7 (1 in 2.3) within 1.5 s. If this recording is typical, exact 95% ranges are 29.0-96.3% and 9.9-81.6% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.6-11.7 and 0.6-8.8 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

1 serious near-miss involved a car at 57.2 km/h with 0.6 s between the person and the vehicle on the same spot. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 14.7% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A 2nd serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 39.7 km/h with 0.4 s between the person and the vehicle on the same spot. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.5% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

A 3rd serious near-miss involved a car at 39.9 km/h with 0.4 s between the person and the vehicle on the same spot. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 3.5% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

1 close pass involved a car at 36.9 km/h with 1.5 s between the person and the vehicle on the same spot.

A 2nd close pass involved a car at 53.1 km/h with 2.8 s between the person and the vehicle on the same spot.

In engineering terms, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video; this one is 2.0 minutes with 7 pedestrian crossings and 22 moving vehicles counted. 82.4% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, based on 8 gaps, 2 of them 12 s or more, longest 36.3 s, with the first and last gaps cut short by the video.

We request that you provide a raised zebra crossing at the Orchard Lane crossing.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) measurements for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

We commissioned a video survey of the crossing. In 26.8 minutes of video, equivalent to 1608.0 s, we recorded 29 crossings and 11 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 27.8 km/h. Parents see the same danger here at each school dismissal. The analysis found 1 serious near-miss and 1 close pass, where serious means pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart and close pass means 1.5 to 3.0 s apart. There was 1 gap of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed and 0 gaps of 12 s or more, with the longest gap 6.9 s. 93.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more. The first and last gaps are cut short by the video. PV² was calculated as 0.0 x 10^8 from 65 pedestrians and 25 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 26.8 minutes of video. A formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count one person twice at 1.3x the true count in our drone test.

The most serious near-miss had a post-encroachment time of 0.4 s when a van passed at 24.5 km/h. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk is 0.9% from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts. rows.letter:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at North Avenue crossing

We write to request a raised zebra crossing at the North Avenue crossing used by our school.

A Crossing Watch video recorded 7.6 minutes (456.0 s) at the site and counted 9 pedestrian crossings and 12 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 59.7 km/h. In 456.0 s of video there were 12 moving vehicles and 9 pedestrian crossings recorded.

In that recording 4 of 9 crossings (1 in 2.2) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s of the person and 2 of 9 (1 in 4.5) within 1.5 s. If this recording is typical, exact 95% ranges are 13.7-78.8% and 2.8-60.0% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

Of the 4 events within 3 s, 2 were serious (less than 1.5 s apart) and 2 were close passes (1.5-3.0 s).

One serious event had a car at 51.1 km/h with 0.3 s between pedestrian and vehicle on the same spot.
That speed carries an adult death risk of 9.1% if hit by a car front (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+), compared with 0.6% at an impact speed of 20.0 km/h.
A second serious event had a van at 27.7 km/h with 1.3 s between pedestrian and vehicle.
That speed carries an adult death risk of 1.2% if hit, compared with 0.2% at 10.0 km/h.
One close pass had a bus at 57.0 km/h with 2.2 s between pedestrian and vehicle.
That speed carries an adult death risk of 2.3% if hit.
A second close pass had a car at 19.7 km/h with 1.8 s between pedestrian and vehicle.
That speed carries an adult death risk of 0.2% if hit, compared with 0.2% at 9.5 km/h.
The time gaps are post-encroachment times from SAM tracking and road-plane geometry, and the individual road user was not reviewed.

The video also showed 43.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, from 10 gaps with 4 of them 12 s or more and the longest 82.5 s.
We note the first and last gaps are cut short by the video, and that PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video while this recording is 7.6 minutes with 9 crossings and 12 vehicles, so those rates should be treated with caution.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location to slow traffic and establish priority for pedestrians.

We are willing to share the video and underlying measurements on request.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

Dear Sir/Madam,

We write concerning Orchard Lane crossing. In 28.8 minutes (1728.0 s) of video we recorded 24 crossings and 17 vehicles. The recording showed 3 serious near-misses defined as less than 1.5 s apart and 1 close pass defined as 1.5-3.0 s. One serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 32.1 km/h with a PET of 0.7 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+).

A second serious near-miss involved a bus at 31.6 km/h with a PET of 0.9 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 1.7%.

A third serious near-miss involved an auto-rickshaw at 19.7 km/h with a PET of 1.4 s. The adult death risk if hit by a car front at that speed is 0.6%.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal

A serious near-miss is defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and a close pass is 1.5 to 3.0 s. In that period we recorded 4 serious near-misses and 2 close passes, with 3 person-first, 2 vehicle-first and 1 both at once.

One serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s with a car at 55.9 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 13.4%).
Another serious near-miss had a PET of 1.2 s with a car at 48.0 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 7.1%).
A third serious near-miss had a PET of 1.0 s with a car at 45.2 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 5.6%).
A fourth serious near-miss had a PET of 0.0 s with a car at 20.0 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 0.6%).
One close pass had a PET of 1.8 s with a van at 24.9 km/h (adult death risk if hit by a car front 0.4%).
Death-risk figures are for adults hit by a car front from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+.

rows.letter:
To the Road Authority,

I write about the safety of the Garden Road crossing outside our school. In a 7.0 minutes video lasting 420.0 s, 7 pedestrian crossings and 10 moving vehicles were counted, with an 85th percentile speed of 52.3 km/h.

The review found 3 serious near-misses, defined as pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 0 close passes of 1.5-3.0 s. All 3 were vehicle first, with 0 person first and 0 both at once.

A bus at 49.8 km/h was 0.5 s from a pedestrian, carrying 8.2% adult death risk if hit by a car front, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h impact. A car at 40.0 km/h was 0.1 s from a pedestrian, carrying 3.6% adult death risk if hit by a car front, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h impact. A bus at 35.8 km/h was 0.1 s from a pedestrian, carrying 2.5% adult death risk if hit by a car front, compared with 0.6% at 20.0 km/h impact. Death risks are from Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts.

On engineering context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video while this one is 7.0. In that video, 81.3% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more, from 9 gaps with 4 of them 12 s or more and longest 61.3 s. Many parents have told us they now avoid the Garden Road crossing because they feel it is too dangerous during school hours.

I request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location. We are happy to share the video for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
